lead: A quantum dot is a semiconductor crystal a few nanometres across. A nanotube is a sheet of carbon atoms rolled into a cylinder. Both are nanomaterials, but their behaviour comes from geometry. In a quantum dot, size sets the band gap and the colour of light absorbed or emitted. In a nanotube, the roll direction, called chirality, decides whether it is metallic or semiconducting. These materials appear in displays, sensors, bioimaging, strong composites and small transistors. Only a few universities teach this as a full topic.
prereq: You need: 6.1 for size-dependent properties and 6.4 for band gap; the Unit 1 particle in a box is the model for confinement.

blocks.text: A quantum dot is a semiconductor crystal with all three dimensions below about 10 nm. Electrons and holes inside it cannot move freely. They are confined like a particle in a box. Confinement turns a continuous band into discrete levels and raises the lowest electron level above the highest hole level. The separation is the band gap, E<sub>g</sub>.

blocks.where: E is photon energy in eV or J; h is Planck's constant; c is speed of light; λ is wavelength; E<sub>g</sub> is band gap.

blocks.text: A smaller dot gives stronger confinement, a larger E<sub>g</sub>, a higher photon energy and a shorter wavelength. So small CdSe dots emit blue light and larger dots emit red. The semiconductor material sets the rough range: CdSe and InP cover visible light, PbS covers infrared.
Uses include QLED displays, bioimaging labels, photodetectors, sensors and solar cells. In a display, dot size is chosen to set each pixel colour.

A carbon nanotube is graphene rolled into a cylinder. A single-walled nanotube (SWCNT) has one wall; a multi-walled nanotube (MWCNT) has several nested cylinders. The roll is fixed by two integers (n, m). Armchair tubes have (n, n); zigzag tubes have (n, 0); all other pairs are chiral.

In the simple zone-folding picture, a tube is metallic when n − m is divisible by 3, and semiconducting otherwise. Armchair tubes are metallic. A zigzag tube is metallic only when n is a multiple of 3. This is why chirality, not only diameter, decides electrical type.
Nanotubes are very strong and conduct heat and electricity well. They are used in polymer composites, field-effect transistors, gas sensors and conductive films. See Unit 5 for composite processing.

The strength comes from the carbon-carbon bond network; the electrical behaviour comes from how the π electrons wrap around the cylinder. A batch of nanotubes is usually a mixture, so separation by type is a practical problem.

Nanomaterials are used because small size gives high surface area and tunable electronic structure. Common uses: displays and lighting; drug delivery carriers; catalysts; gas and biosensors; energy storage in batteries and supercapacitors (see Unit 4).

Quantum dots are chosen when colour tuning matters. Nanotubes are chosen when strength, conductivity or a tiny channel matters. Metal and metal-oxide nanoparticles are common catalysts and sensors. Porous nanomaterials store ions in batteries and supercapacitors.

Catalysis is a large near-term use: more surface atoms mean more active sites per gram. The same property can be a risk: high surface area also means high reactivity, and small particles can enter the body. Applications therefore need control of size, shape, purity and surface coating, as covered in 6.1 and 6.2.

examples.question: A CdSe quantum dot emits light of wavelength 600 nm. Find the photon energy in eV. Use hc = 1240 eV·nm.
steps: Write the data: λ = 600 nm and hc = 1240 eV·nm.
The unit nm cancels: E = 2.0667 eV.
Round to two decimal places: E = 2.07 eV.
examples.check:
hc = 1240.0
lam = 600.0
E = hc / lam
print(round(E, 2))

traps: Smaller dot → larger gap → shorter wavelength (bluer). Reversing this is the common error.
Photon energy is inversely proportional to wavelength: 600 nm is lower energy than 500 nm.
Band gap may be in eV or J, and wavelength in nm; convert units before dividing.
Chirality (n, m) matters: an armchair tube is metallic, but not every nanotube is.
High surface area is not the same as high band gap; size effects and surface effects are different.

quiz.a: A semiconductor crystal with all dimensions below about 10 nm.

quiz.q: Why does a smaller quantum dot emit bluer light?
quiz.a: Stronger confinement raises the band gap; the emitted photon has higher energy and shorter wavelength.

quiz.q: A dot emits at 500 nm. Find photon energy using hc = 1240 eV·nm.
Two CdSe dots, 3 nm and 5 nm. Which emits longer wavelength and why?
quiz.a: The 5 nm dot; weaker confinement gives a smaller gap, lower photon energy and longer wavelength.

quiz.q: Name two types of carbon nanotube.
What does chirality decide in a nanotube?
quiz.a: Whether the simple tube is metallic or semiconducting, and the atomic arrangement.

quiz.q: A nanotube has (n, m) = (6, 3). Metallic or semiconducting in the simple rule?
quiz.a: n − m = 3, divisible by 3, so it is metallic.

beyond: Not for the exam. Quantum-dot displays and photodetectors are commercial; research focuses on cadmium-free dots such as InP and on infrared PbS dots. Carbon-nanotube transistors and conductive films are active areas, with separation of metallic and semiconducting tubes as a key step. Search next for 'quantum dot display', 'chirality-selective nanotube separation' and 'carbon nanotube composite'.
